records.title: Cystic fibrosis in China: addressing the cycle of underdiagnosis and treatment inaccessibility.
records.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is substantially underdiagnosed in China, and access to targeted therapy remains limited. Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) modulator therapy has dramatically improved survival internationally, yet none has been approved or entered clinical trials in China. A circular problem contributes to this situation: CF is not included in newborn screening programmes because it has historically been considered extremely rare in East Asian populations. Yet, fewer than 300 patients have been genetically confirmed, in part due to limited diagnostic infrastructure. Epidemiological data based on carrier frequency suggest the true affected population exceeds 17,000 individuals. Patients who receive a molecular diagnosis face additional challenges, including a CFTR variant spectrum that differs from Western populations without established theratyping pathways, and the absence of regulatory submissions for CFTR modulators. Here, we discuss three potential approaches: expanding diagnostic capacity through standardised sweat chloride testing and clinician education, building theratyping infrastructure via patient-derived organoid biobanks, and applying existing rare disease regulatory pathways to facilitate drug approval.

records.title: Stress-induced alterations in neurodevelopment in iPSC-Derived i n vitro model systems.
records.abstract: Psychological stress is common in women during pregnancy and after childbirth, showing a prevalence of up to 15.6% in pregnant women in developing countries. Clinical and pre-clinical studies have implicated their role in negatively affecting pregnancy outcomes and have been linked to adverse child outcomes. Yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, specifically the signatures associated with their effect on human fetal development. Thereby, impairing our further understanding of the effects of therapeutics used to treat these disorders in expecting mothers. This study proposes the use of human iPSC-derived embryoid bodies (EBs) and forebrain-specific organoids as complementary human developmental models to investigate the effects of exposure to prenatal stress (mediated by glucocorticoids) across distinct stages, in vitro. Our findings suggested that excessive glucocorticoids altered early lineage specification in an exposure-dependent manner. This was evidenced by a brief increase in pluripotent and neural progenitor populations, with mild alterations in proliferative dynamics without a net change in proliferative capacity. Changes in lineage-associated markers were observed in ectodermal and meso-endodermal layers of EBs. Particularly, focusing on neurogenesis (forebrain-specific organoids) to understand the impact of stress on neurodevelopment, we saw concentration-dependent changes in progenitor maintenance and neuronal- glial differentiation. Furthermore, the activation of inflammatory and oxidative stress responses can be implicated as signalling mechanisms responsible for the differences observed. Together, these results suggest that glucocorticoid signalling linked to prenatal stress can alter developmental trajectories by modifying cellular states rather than directly altering proliferation or survival during early development.

records.title: Modern cell-based assays for biomedical research: from conventional methods to AI-driven high content analysis.
records.abstract: In vitro cell-based assays are fundamental tools in biomedical research, supporting investigations of cellular physiology, disease mechanisms, drug discovery, toxicology, regenerative medicine, and precision therapeutics. However, conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell culture models often fail to recapitulate the structural complexity and physiological functions of native tissues, prompting the development of advanced platforms, including three-dimensional (3D) cultures, organoids, organ-on-a-chip technologies, and microphysiological systems. Recent advances in cell viability and cytotoxicity assessment, functional cellular analysis, molecular profiling, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-based functional genomics, high-content imaging, flow cytometry, single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and automated high-throughput screening have expanded the analytical capabilities of cell-based assays. Furthermore, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image analysis and computational biology has enhanced cellular phenotyping, biomarker discovery, and mechanistic investigation, with the potential to improve the prediction of therapeutic efficacy and toxicity. Nevertheless, challenges related to physiological relevance, technical variability, inadequate standardization, high operational costs, scalability, poor reproducibility, cell-line misidentification, batch-to-batch variation, and inconsistent reporting continue to hinder translational applications. Future progress will depend on integrating physiologically relevant models with AI-driven analytics, spatial multi-omics, digital pathology, automated screening, and microphysiological systems. Standardized protocols, harmonized reporting practices, and interdisciplinary collaboration will be essential to improve reproducibility, strengthen regulatory acceptance, advance precision medicine, and reduce reliance on animal experimentation. In this context, this review critically evaluates conventional and emerging in vitro cell-based assays, emphasizing their biological principles, analytical capabilities, translational applications, and practical limitations, while highlighting future opportunities to improve predictive accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical translation.

records.title: Engineering Human Blood Vessel Organoids for Failed Ischemic Repair in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
records.abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) remains a major cause of nonhealing wounds, tissue loss, amputation, and death despite advances in revascularization. This Review reframes CLTI as failed ischemic vascularized-tissue repair and evaluates how human vascular models can reproduce disease-specific repair failure and test regenerative interventions. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from human CLTI with experimental studies of human blood vessel organoids (BVOs), engineered perfusable microvessels, vascular-on-chip systems, and vascularized tissue models. Direct CLTI observations are distinguished from mechanisms inferred from related ischemic, metabolic, and inflammatory systems. Model requirements and readouts are organized around disease-specific pathological benchmarks. The synthesis indicates that restoration of macroscopic blood flow may be insufficient when microvascular maturation, tissue perfusion, and reparative remodeling remain defective. CLTI-oriented platforms should therefore reproduce sustained hypoperfusion, heterogeneous hypoxia, metabolic dysfunction, persistent inflammation, diabetes-associated microvascular injury, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and failed vascular maturation. BVOs are best positioned as the vascular core of modular ischemic-limb systems integrated, when required, with skeletal-muscle, wound, stromal, immune, matrix, and neural compartments. The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-lactate-lactylation relationship is presented as a proposed, testable framework connecting oxygen sensing, glycolytic remodeling, lactate accumulation, endothelial and immune plasticity, and unstable vascular repair. A platform-specific roadmap combines patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells, microfluidic perfusion, multicellular coculture, multi-omic profiling, and structural, maturation, functional, durability, and tissue-repair endpoints. BVO-based and perfusion-enabled vascular platforms can support mechanistic validation, therapeutic and toxicity screening, patient-specific modeling, and vascularized construct design, provided that structural angiogenesis is distinguished from functional and durable tissue rescue.

records.title: Comparison of TNFα, IFNγ, and DSS in modeling inflammatory bowel disease in murine enteroids and assessment of the role of zonulin inhibitor larazotide acetate.
records.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by chronic inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract. We hypothesized that the zonulin inhibitor larazotide acetate (LA), designed to regulate loss of tight junctions between intestinal cells and currently used for the treatment of celiac disease, could also have potential therapeutic value in the treatment of IBD. BALB/c enteroids were exposed to dextran sulfate sodium (DSS), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNFα), or interferon-gamma (IFNγ) for 48 h to induce an IBD-like environment, followed by treatment with LA. Organoids were assessed for intestinal permeability, viability, and expression of the zonulin (Hp), occludin (Ocln), zonula occludens-1 (Zo1), and intestinal stem cell marker (Lgr5) genes. Enteroids harbored Lgr5+ intestinal stem cells, Muc2+ goblet cells, chromogranin A+ enteroendocrine cells, and lysozyme+ Paneth cells. DSS-, TNFα-, or IFNγ-treated enteroids displayed increased intestinal permeability and loss of epithelial barrier function. While DSS activated apoptotic pathways, exposure to high doses of TNFα and IFNγ resulted in necrosis. DSS-related RNA degradation prevented the assessment of its effects on gene expression in enteroids. Treatment with TNFα, but not IFNγ, induced an increase in zonulin (Hp) expression that could be counteracted by LA. IBD can be mimicked in vitro best using TNFα. LA showed potential for the treatment of IBD induced by TNFα, but it should be used with caution in highly inflammatory environments.

records.title: Establishment of lung cancer organoid lines from malignant pleural effusion: medium optimization and specimen quality-control analysis.
records.abstract: Lung cancer organoids (LCO) derived from malignant pleural effusion (MPE) offer unique advantages for modeling advanced disease, but existing methods suffer from variable success rates and limited capacity for long-term culture, hindering the establishment of stable organoid lines. Here, we systematically optimized the generation of MPE-derived LCO lines through a dual-strategy approach. Medium supplementation with 10%-25% pleural effusion supernatant (PES) significantly promoted organoid growth. Analysis of 35 clinicopathological parameters identified hemorrhagic effusion, positive liquid-based cytology and positive cell block as factors associated with successful organoid establishment. In a multivariable model, hemorrhagic effusion (adjusted OR 3.47, 95% CI 1.18-10.2) and positive liquid-based cytology (adjusted OR 6.92, 95% CI 1.43-33.4) remained associated with success after adjustment, though these exploratory findings require external validation. Using this optimized system, we successfully generated 30 lung cancer organoid lines representing major histological subtypes, demonstrating the broad applicability of our method. Collectively, this study establishes an efficient workflow for generating LCO lines from malignant pleural effusion, providing a useful technical basis for downstream applications.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction.
records.abstract: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

records.title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
records.abstract: To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: Efficient and Accurate Zero Shot Generation of Symmetric Protein Complexes.
records.abstract: Symmetric organization is a fundamental principle of biomolecular complex assembly. The same principle underlies engineered applications, from vaccine platforms to nanomaterials, making symmetric de novo generation a core capability for computational protein design. We establish a theoretical foundation equating generation of an assembly with underlying symmetry group $G$ to generation within a quotient space over $G$. This directly allows $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant models to generate symmetric structures with minimal distribution shift. With this insight we introduce ZeUS ($\textbf{Ze}$ro-shot $\textbf{U}$nified $\textbf{S}$ymmetrization), a framework that converts any pretrained $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant backbone generative model into an efficient generator of symmetric assemblies with no retraining. ZeUS operates on a single $\textit{canonical subunit}$ and utilizes $\textit{phantom subunits}$ to preserve internal model operations, reducing memory and runtime cost by $\mathcal{O}(|G|)$ for finite groups $G$, compared to a full-complex forward pass. We implement ZeUS for IPA-based models (FrameDiff, FoldFlow) and axial-attention-based RFdiffusion, showing high generation efficiency with minimal degradation to generation quality. We then apply ZeUS to generate symmetric complexes of over $10{,}000$ residues with exact, untruncated attention, a scale previously intractable with any model.

records.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme.
records.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((kcat/KM)/kw) of up to 3 x 1013 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

records.title: AlphaInterp: Revealing how AlphaFold 3 processes structure, confidence, and evolutionary information.
records.abstract: How does evolutionary information become structural knowledge? AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with remarkable accuracy, yet how it transforms comparative sequence information into three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. Here, we use mechanistic interpretability to follow this transformation through AlphaFold 3 and identify a computational principle underlying its structural inference. By extracting single- and pair-representations across the model's forward pass and combining representational-geometry analysis, linear probing, activation patching, and perturbation of the multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and its phylogenetic diversity, we show that AlphaFold 3 does not simply infer structure from raw sequence nor from MSA depth. Instead, a small number of sufficiently divergent homologues provides enough comparative information to largely recover the structure predicted using the full MSA. The pairformer transforms this evolutionary signal into a compact latent space in which residue-pair distances, contacts, fold similarity, and structural confidence become progressively decodable. Removing the MSA disrupts these latent geometries. Replacing it with evolutionarily similar homologues provides substantially less information, while evolutionarily unrelated sequences fail to rescue prediction despite preserving the formal alignment input. In contrast, phylogenetically diverse MSA subsampling largely restores both prediction accuracy and representational coherence. These results suggest that AlphaFold 3 has learned to infer structure by constraining its geometric priors and structural hypotheses by the sequence variation of the MSA. This framework helps explain both the model's remarkable predictive power and its characteristic failure modes, with direct implications for protein design, conformational diversity, out-of-distribution generalization, and the interpretation of model confidence.

records.title: Computational identification and comparative characterization of ligand scaffolds for VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 kinase domains in neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
records.abstract: VEGFR-1 and VEGFR-2 have distinct but complementary roles in vascular endothelial growth factor signaling, providing a rationale for comparing ligand recognition by their kinase domains in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. We integrated dual-receptor docking, fragment tree Transformer-based variational autoencoder generation, and three-dimensional Monte Carlo tree search to identify candidate ligand scaffolds. Screening 37,445 natural product-like structures retained 989 compounds, and subsequent molecular generation and physicochemical filtering produced 1,315 structures for receptor-constrained optimization. Twenty candidates were prioritized, of which VDS-1, VDS-2, and VDS-3 were examined using three independent 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations per complex and MM/PBSA analysis. VDS-1 showed the most negative MM/PBSA estimates for VEGFR-2 (-49.79 ± 0.21 kcal/mol) and VEGFR-1 (-45.95 ± 1.84 kcal/mol), whereas VDS-2 exhibited substantial between-trajectory variability. VDS-3 showed limited between-trajectory variation in its MM/PBSA estimates for both receptors, although protein-aligned ligand RMSD revealed between-replicate heterogeneity, particularly in VEGFR-1. Van der Waals interactions predominated among favorable modeled contributions, with PHE1047 in VEGFR-2 and ILE881 in VEGFR-1 emerging as recurrent interaction regions. Although VDS-1 showed favorable modeled interactions, it had substantial physicochemical and predicted safety liabilities. VDS-3 therefore represented a comparatively balanced starting scaffold for further optimization, although experimental validation and toxicity assessment remain necessary.

records.title: Reprogramming Protein Function by Expanding Chemical and Combinatorial Space: Integrating Chemical and Computational Strategies.
records.abstract: Proteins are biological macromolecules that perform critical functions, including catalysis, molecular recognition, and cellular regulation. Natural evolution has generated remarkable protein diversity, leaving vast opportunities for engineered molecular innovation. Protein engineering has evolved from the rational design of proteins over the last few decades to approaches based on directed evolution and computational methods to enhance their properties. Protein engineering is shifting from optimization-based approaches to an integrated approach, which includes rational design, directed evolution, computational and generative modeling, synthetic chemistry, synthetic biology, and laboratory automation. These strategies widen the scope of experimentally accessible chemical and structural toolboxes in proteins without sacrificing the physicochemical constraints, cellular compatibility, evolutionary processes, and experimental validation. Meanwhile, synthetic chemistry is extending the natural abilities of proteins by incorporating noncanonical amino acids, novel cofactors, and modified metal centers and catalytic environments. These technologies enable the creation of artificial enzymes, programmed molecular binders, synthetic receptors, molecular machines, and biomaterials that have functions beyond those of their natural counterparts. This review introduces advances in the protein engineering field, from past methods of modifying proteins to present-day opportunities for generating proteins with artificial intelligence, and explains how the fields of computation, chemistry, and biology are driving the future of programmable proteins.

records.title: Recent advances in fabrication strategies, functional modulation and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels.
records.abstract: Native protein-based hydrogels not only possess all advantages of their denatured analogues such as exceptional biocompatibility and low toxicity, but also retain the intrinsic function of the protein building block. Therefore, they exhibit novel favorable properties including inherent bioactivity and reversible sol-gel transformation behavior. As such, they have emerged as versatile biomaterials widely used in the biomedical field. This review provides a comprehensive and up-to date overview of design strategies, formation mechanisms, and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels. We systematically summarize the key cross-linking strategies for fabricating reversible native protein-based hydrogels, with particular emphasis on how these interactions govern hydrogel formation and their functionality. We highlight recent advances in fabricating these hydrogels through chemical cross-linking, physical cross-linking, metal coordination, fusion protein design, key interface redesign, de novo design, and modular design strategies, which enable precise control over hierarchical architecture, stimuli-responsiveness, and biomechanical properties. Furthermore, we explore the diverse healthcare applications of these hydrogels, with emphasis on drug delivery, wound healing, and tissue engineering. Finally, we discuss perspectives on future directions, including the integration of computational modeling, machine learning, and high-throughput experimentation to enable rational design of smart, multifunctional native protein-based hydrogels with tailored performances for next-generation biomedical applications.

records.title: EPIGEN-Prostate: Identifying multi-omic markers of prostate cancer in Aotearoa New Zealand men.
records.abstract: DNA methylation biomarkers have demonstrated promise as potential clinical biomarkers for improved detection and risk stratification of prostate cancer (PCa). Despite this, only sparse genome-scale, sequencing-based DNA methylation data are available in the early PCa setting. The EPIGEN-Prostate study aims to identify novel cell-free DNA methylation biomarkers from blood and multi-omic biomarkers from prostate tissue for detecting clinically significant PCa (csPCa). EPIGEN-Prostate is a multi-centre, prospective, longitudinal cohort study of patients undergoing investigation for potential PCa, with a biomarker discovery-focused design. The primary objective of this study is to characterise novel cell-free DNA-based molecular biomarkers for non-invasive PCa detection and risk stratification. Secondary objectives include the development of multi-omic risk classifiers to predict disease progression and treatment response. The primary endpoint is the presence or absence of csPCa, defined here as International Society of Urological Pathology grade group ≥2. Secondary endpoints will include disease stage at presentation, disease recurrence following curative treatment, metastasis-free survival, and overall survival. Individuals aged ≥18 years, scheduled to undergo prostate biopsy, and able to provide informed consent are eligible to participate. Blood samples will be prospectively collected before prostate biopsy, and prostate biopsy tissue will be retrieved for analysis after regular processing. Participants proceeding to radical prostatectomy may contribute surgical tissue and serial postoperative blood samples. Pre-biopsy plasma and matched prostate tissue samples will undergo genome-wide DNA methylation profiling using reduced representation bisulfite sequencing approaches. Tissue samples will also undergo RNA sequencing and genetic profiling. Clinical outcomes will be collected for up to 15 years. Biomarker discovery and validation will integrate molecular and clinical data using nested case-control analyses for each objective. Not applicable. Human ethical approval was obtained via the New Zealand Health and Disability Ethics Committee - Southern (HDEC 21/STH/184).

records.title: Circulating tumor cells in solid tumors: biological adaptation, detection technologies, and clinical implications.
records.abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are rare tumor-derived cells released from primary or metastatic lesions into the bloodstream and represent key intermediates in hematogenous dissemination. As intact cellular components of liquid biopsy, CTCs provide opportunities to investigate tumor heterogeneity, metastatic evolution, therapeutic resistance, and dynamic molecular alterations that may not be fully captured by tissue biopsy or circulating cell-free analytes. This review summarizes current advances in the biological mechanisms, detection technologies, and clinical applications of CTCs in solid tumors, with particular emphasis on their adaptive responses within the circulation. CTCs exhibit substantial phenotypic and metabolic plasticity, including epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, altered energy metabolism, and enhanced resistance to oxidative and mechanical stress. Their interactions with platelets, neutrophils, and other immune components can further promote survival, immune evasion, and metastatic competence, particularly through the formation of homotypic and heterotypic CTC clusters. Technological advances in antigen-independent enrichment, microfluidic isolation, single-cell multi-omics, and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis are progressively extending CTC assessment beyond enumeration toward molecular and functional characterization. Emerging clinical evidence supports the potential value of CTCs for prognostic stratification, treatment monitoring, and biomarker assessment in breast, lung, prostate, colorectal, and head and neck cancers, although clinical utility varies considerably among tumor types and platforms. Further standardization and prospective validation, together with integration of metabolic, immune, and multi-omic CTC features, will be essential to establish their role in precision oncology.

records.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions.
records.abstract: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions. We applied a pre-trained deep learning model to brightfield images of single cells from malignant effusions of 10 patients with metastatic breast cancer to extract morphological features, quantify tumor cell fraction (TCF), and guide label-free microfluidic enrichment. We profiled copy-number alterations and somatic mutations in enriched tumor cell fractions and compared them with available matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors. AI-powered single-cell morphological analysis identified putative tumor cells in all 10 patients (median TCF, 5.4%; range, 0.51-15.8%; n = 25 samples). AI estimates of major immune-cell populations varied across patients and samples and correlated with flow cytometry measurements (n = 21 paired samples, Pearson r = 0.69-0.75). Unsupervised analysis identified four tumor cell morphotypes, revealing intra- and inter-patient morphological heterogeneity and longitudinal variation in morphotype composition. Genomic profiling of enriched tumor cell fractions by low-pass whole-genome sequencing (n = 26 samples) and whole-exome sequencing (n = 24 samples) identified copy-number alterations and somatic mutations, with tumor fraction influencing genomic signal strength. Comparisons of genomic profiles from tumor cell-enriched fractions with matched effusion cell-free DNA and solid tumors revealed shared genomic alterations, providing orthogonal support for tumor origin and relatedness, while differences across analytes revealed genomic divergence and tumor heterogeneity. AI-powered analysis leverages single-cell morphology for tumor cell identification and label-free enrichment, while integration with genomic profiling enables simultaneous interrogation of phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions. This approach expands the potential of malignant effusions for liquid biopsy applications and biomarker development and discovery.

records.title: Glycans on Tumor-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for Cancer Liquid Biopsy: From Signatures to Selective Capture.
records.abstract: Tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (tdEVs) are stable carriers of tumor-associated information in biofluids and have emerged as promising minimally invasive biomarkers for cancer detection and monitoring. While protein and nucleic acid cargo have been extensively characterized, the glycosylation landscape of tdEVs remains largely underexplored. Surface-accessible glycans can be displayed across multiple glycoprotein and glycolipid scaffolds, potentially increasing targetable epitope density and enabling direct detection or enrichment of intact vesicles. Across cancer types, tumor-associated EVs display recurrent glycan alterations, including altered fucosylation and sialylation, alongside cancer-associated structures such as truncated O-glycans, glycosphingolipids, and oncofetal chondroitin sulfate. These glycan alterations may reflect the malignant state of the cells from which the EVs originate, while certain EV-associated glycans may also contribute to tumor progression. This review synthesizes current evidence on tdEV glycosylation across major glycan classes and critically evaluates the technical and biological challenges that limit clinical translation of EV-associated glycans as cancer biomarkers. We propose a conceptual framework in which cancer-enriched glycans are best exploited through structurally resolved multiplexed signatures, while cancer-restricted glycans such as truncated O-glycans and oncofetal chondroitin sulfate serve as tumor-selective capture handles for downstream patient-specific cargo profiling. Addressing methodological standardization and validation gaps will be essential to realize the potential of glycan-based tdEV assays in precision oncology.

records.title: Real-world comparison of routine and companion diagnostic mismatch repair immunohistochemistry in a large Chinese pan-tumour cohort.
records.abstract: DNA mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry (IHC) is widely used for Lynch syndrome screening and selection of patients for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Standardized companion diagnostic (CDx) testing and interpretation frameworks support consistent patient classification. We evaluated routine clinical-record MMR IHC results against the Food and Drug Administration-approved CDx, VENTANA MMR RxDx Panel (Roche Diagnostics), and examined focal staining and reduced-protein testing strategies. This retrospective multicentre study included 1443 resection specimens from five hospitals in China: colorectal carcinoma (CRC; n = 402), endometrial carcinoma (EC; n = 413), gastric carcinoma (GC; n = 367) and other solid tumours (n = 261). Concordance between historical clinical-record MMR status and the CDx classification varied by tumour type. The highest agreement was observed in CRC and GC, whereas EC and the heterogeneous other-tumour subgroup showed the lowest positive per cent agreement (95.81%) and the lowest negative per cent agreement (92.98%), respectively. Third-panel assessment of 34 discordant cases supported the VENTANA classification in 31 cases, while the three remaining cases were unresolved without orthogonal molecular testing. Subclonal loss was identified in 74 of 525 dMMR cases (14.1%; most in MSH6 and MLH1), highlighting interpretative complexity beyond a binary framework. Reduced two-protein testing, although operationally attractive, may miss clinically meaningful dMMR cases: the best-performing PMS2/MSH6 combination was estimated to miss 33 dMMR cases when assessed against the VENTANA four-protein classification. These findings support full-panel MMR assessment and adherence to CDx-specific interpretation guidance to improve confidence in patient selection for ICI therapy.

records.title: Cell-free DNA-guided detection, surveillance, and therapeutic adaptation for breast cancer.
records.abstract: Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) analysis provides a minimally invasive approach to breast cancer assessment across early detection, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and treatment adaptation in advanced disease. This review evaluates these applications by distinguishing analytical validity, clinical detection performance, prognostic validity, and clinical utility. In early detection, assays integrating genomic, epigenomic, fragmentomic, and protein-based features have shown encouraging performance in evaluated cohorts; however, sensitivity remains limited in low-burden disease, particularly stage I breast cancer. Their potential clinical role depends on the incremental information they provide beyond established imaging and diagnostic pathways. In the curative-intent setting, circulating tumor DNA detection after treatment is associated with recurrence risk and can precede clinical or radiographic relapse, supporting prognostic stratification and the design of MRD-guided intervention trials. Whether such interventions improve clinical outcomes remains a central unresolved question. In advanced breast cancer, plasma genotyping supports treatment selection in defined molecular contexts. Randomized trials of ESR1 mutation-guided endocrine switching have demonstrated progression-free survival benefits with specific treatment strategies, providing evidence beyond biomarker-outcome associations, although overall survival benefit remains to be established. Across applications, interpretation depends on assay characteristics, molecular input, disease setting, sampling schedule, and the clinical decision being evaluated. Future studies should connect assay performance to patient benefit through comparison with existing care, clinically meaningful endpoints, and assessment of treatment burden and downstream investigations. This approach will help define where cfDNA testing can contribute meaningfully to breast cancer management.
